title: Groin ultrasound (hernia)
what: The doctor looks at your groin with ultrasound to check for a hernia, a bulge through a weak spot in the belly wall.
why: For a swelling or pain in the groin, especially when coughing or straining. In children, if a lump appears in the groin.
duration: usually 10 to 20 minutes; the report is usually ready right away
tell_doctor: When the swelling appears, and if it goes away when you lie down
If the pain got strong or the lump will no longer go back in

prepare.title: Preparation
prepare.text: Usually none. You can eat and drink.

prepare.title: Clothing
prepare.text: Comfortable clothes that make it easy to uncover your groin.

prepare.title: For children
prepare.text: If the scan is for a child, explain that there will be cool gel and it does not hurt. Bring a toy.

steps: You lie on your back and uncover your groin
Gel is put on your skin
The doctor moves the probe on the right and left
You are asked to cough or strain
Sometimes you are also checked standing up
feel: Cool gel and light pressure from the probe
A little awkward. That is normal
after: The report is usually ready right away
If a hernia is found, a surgeon will tell you if and when you need surgery
red_flags: A lump in the groin became hard and painful and will not go away: call emergency services
Groin pain with vomiting and a swollen belly: call emergency services

faq.a: Coughing raises pressure in the belly, so a hernia shows up better.

faq.q: Can a hernia go away on its own?
faq.a: In adults, usually not. But not every hernia needs urgent surgery. A surgeon decides.

reminders.text: Groin ultrasound tomorrow. No preparation needed. Wear comfortable clothes.
